title: Bride of the Monster

evidence.note: No renewal search was completed. A catalog script flagged an entry: RE0000216687 (1984), 'Bride of the monster', claimant Packing Service Corporation (Sidney Barton). Nobody opened that record, because publicrecords.copyright.gov needs an interactive search, and no Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volume was found. It is not confirmed that the entry is this film. A 1984 registration also falls outside the normal renewal window for a 1955 work (1982-1983), so it may be a late or unrelated filing, and its legal effect is unresolved until the record is read. The print stays undetermined. Wikipedia says the ending credits name 'Filmakers Releasing Organization' as the copyright holder.

Wikipedia credits Frank Worth as composer. The soundtrack's copyright was not checked separately. A sound film's recorded track normally shares the film's own status, so it depends on the print question.

Wikipedia credits the writing to Alex Gordon and Ed Wood and names no source material. The screenplay was not checked separately. If it is an original script, it would follow the film's own copyright.
Wikipedia reports that Legend Films released a colorized version in 2008. Colorization is added material that can carry its own copyright, even where the black-and-white original does not.

editorial:
Bride of the Monster is a 1955 science-fiction horror film written by Alex Gordon and Ed Wood. Per Wikipedia, it was made by Rolling M. Productions and premiered at Hollywood's Paramount theater on May 11, 1955. Creators look for it because it is an Ed Wood title that is available online, including an upload on the Internet Archive.

The open question is the copyright renewal. A catalog script flagged a 1984 entry, RE0000216687, titled 'Bride of the monster' and filed by Packing Service Corporation. No renewal search was completed, and nobody could open the record to confirm that it is this film. A 1984 registration for a 1955 film is outside the normal renewal window (1982-1983), so it may be a late or unrelated filing. Its legal effect is unresolved until the record is read. Free availability on the Internet Archive is not a clearance. A 2008 colorized release from Legend Films adds a separate layer. The score and screenplay were not independently checked.
faq: Is Bride of the Monster safe to reuse?

Not confirmed. A 1984 entry, RE0000216687, titled 'Bride of the monster' was flagged. It may be a late or unrelated filing, because 1984 is outside the normal 1982-1983 renewal window for a 1955 film. Its legal effect is unresolved until the record is read. Pull that record from the Copyright Office public records before reusing the film. The score, screenplay, any colorization and any trademark are separate questions.
Can I use the Internet Archive copy or the colorized version?

Hosting on the Internet Archive is not a rights clearance. Do not use the copy until the renewal question is resolved. The 2008 Legend Films colorized version adds material that can have its own copyright, so do not treat it as free either.
